topic: The deepest point of the ocean
hook_candidates: Drop Mount Everest here and it would still be underwater.
Fewer people have been here than to the Moon.
The pressure down here would crush you like a soda can.

scenes.narration: Drop Mount Everest here and it would still be underwater.
This is the Challenger Deep, at the bottom of the Mariana Trench.
scenes.image_prompt: A tiny submarine with a headlight descending into an endless dark blue ocean trench, glowing particles, deep perspective looking down.

scenes.narration: It's almost eleven kilometers down, deeper than Everest is tall.
scenes.image_prompt: Side-by-side cross-section: Mount Everest placed inside an ocean trench, its peak still far below the sea surface.

scenes.narration: The water pushes on you with over 1,000 times the air pressure.
scenes.image_prompt: A deep-sea diver silhouette being squeezed by huge arrows of water pressure from every side, dark ocean.

scenes.narration: That's like an elephant standing on your thumbnail.
scenes.image_prompt: A grey elephant balancing on a giant human thumbnail, comic exaggeration, studio backdrop.

scenes.narration: Sunlight dies after a few hundred meters, so it's pitch black.
scenes.image_prompt: Sun rays fading as they go down into the ocean, the bottom half of the picture pitch black.

scenes.narration: But something still lives down there.
scenes.image_prompt: A strange glowing deep-sea creature with big eyes emerging from darkness.

scenes.narration: Tiny shrimp-like amphipods, and fish made of almost jelly.
scenes.image_prompt: Tiny translucent shrimp-like amphipods and a pale jelly-like snailfish swimming in darkness, bioluminescent glow.

scenes.narration: Fewer people have reached this spot than have walked on the Moon.
scenes.image_prompt: An astronaut on the Moon looking at a lone deep-sea submarine on the ocean floor, split composition.

scenes.narration: And here's the scary part: scientists found plastic bags there too.

And humans still left trash there.
